clue.text: Graves may be found underground here

definitions.text: Graves may be found underground here

parts.words: Graves may be found underground here
parts.note: Graves reads as burial plots in a cemetery, but it is a Bordeaux wine, stored in a cool basement room

explanation.surface: A gloomy hint at where the dead lie buried.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves is a red or white wine from the Bordeaux region; the capital letter is hidden by its place at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement store for bottles is where a Bordeaux such as Graves would be kept below ground.

clue.text: Humorist said as little as possible

indicators.note: said signals that the word for a humorist is heard spoken

parts.note: a wit is a clever humorist

explanation.surface: A comedian who says almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle or jot, as in not caring one jot.

clue.text: Tale from unfamiliar American city is abridged

parts.note: novel means new, unfamiliar
Los Angeles is shortened to its initials

explanation.surface: A story about a strange city in the US is cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: A short novel or longish story.

clue.text: Cut yesterday's joint?

definitions.meaning: to cut someone is to snub or ignore them
a joint of meat roasted yesterday and served chilled, such as lamb from the shoulder

explanation.surface: Slicing up the leftover roast.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate snub and a chilled leftover cut of roast lamb share this phrase.

clue.text: A success with females many lads fancy

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are given an ornamental rearrangement

explanation.surface: Lots of boys are attracted to a popular figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A man popular with women, a charmer.

clue.text: Following stars, yachtsman's beginning to get off course

indicators.note: the yachtsman's initial comes after the Latin stars

parts.note: astra is Latin for stars

indicators.note: the beginning of yachtsman's is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor steers by the stars and still goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link. ASTRA is familiar from the RAF motto Per ardua ad astra.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying away from the correct path or route.

clue.text: For example, the House of Commons mace

definitions.text: For example, the House of Commons
definitions.meaning: Parliament is often jokingly called the best gentlemen's society in London, an exclusive association of members
a mace is a heavy cudgel used as a weapon

explanation.surface: The ceremonial mace carried in Britain's House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A society with members, like Parliament, and a heavy bludgeon share this one word.

clue.text: Like pride shown by one numbered among the Popes

definitions.meaning: a pride is a group of lions, so this means lion-like
a pope called Leo with the number nine, Leo IX

explanation.surface: Pride exhibited by a pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown by' is a link; Pope Leo IX read out gives the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lion-like, as a pride is a group of lions, and the ninth Pope Leo written out.

clue.text: Jet escort provided for scoundrel

parts.note: jet is deep black, as in jet-black
a guard escorts someone

explanation.surface: An aircraft is given a military escort on behalf of a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonourable rogue or villain.

clue.text: Remove power of patient goddess

parts.note: a patient is an invalid, someone ill
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A goddess robs a sick person of strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify something is to strip it of force or legal effect.

clue.text: Article on island state

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: IOW is the abbreviation for the Isle of Wight, an island off southern England
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Writing a newspaper article about the condition of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern member of the United States.

clue.text: One's bound to be entertaining

parts.note: bound reads as certain, but it means tied up: the performer is chained up in order to amuse

explanation.surface: Someone who is certain to be amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer such as Houdini who escapes from chains and locks for an audience.

clue.text: Very rich, having stripped last asset

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for very rich is taken off

parts.note: plush means luxurious, very rich

explanation.surface: A wealthy person forced to sell their last remaining holding.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or point in one's favour is a valuable thing to have.

clue.text: Rebuke and criticism for stage comedy

parts.note: a slap is a rebuke, as in a slap on the wrist
stick is informal for criticism, as in giving someone stick

explanation.surface: A theatre production meets a rebuke and bad reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Boisterous knockabout humour of pratfalls and custard pies performed in theatres.

clue.text: A horse possessing a chance is given star treatment

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the word for horse wraps the word for chance

parts.note: a steed is a horse
a risk is a chance

explanation.surface: A racehorse with an outside chance is treated like a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with the little star-shaped symbol used in print.

clue.text: Like tides or waves on a lake

parts.note: waves stands for seas, the rolling water
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A description of tides and waves on a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides vary with the time of year, springs and neaps following the calendar.

clue.text: Something to eat without which Frenchman's not full?

definitions.text: Something to eat without which Frenchman's not full?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened Frenchman goes around the meal
the word for a Frenchman is incomplete, losing its last letter

parts.note: a Gaul is an inhabitant of ancient France
tea is a meal, something to eat

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is not satisfied until he has had his cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since the Frenchman's meal is incomplete without cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich French cake is something eaten, and the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Messenger bearing the earliest of tidings for royal attendant

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the messenger holds the letter inside

parts.note: a courier is a messenger

indicators.note: the first letter of tidings is taken

explanation.surface: A messenger brings the first news to a member of the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant at a royal court.

clue.text: Embrace sweetheart an indefinite number of times

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
the suffix -fold means times, as in tenfold

explanation.surface: Someone hugs a lover again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap in one's arms or envelop is to hug or hold close.

clue.text: Pigeon followers

parts.note: fans are followers, devotees
a tail is someone who follows, shadowing a suspect

explanation.surface: Pigeons that follow people around.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of domestic dove with a spread fan-shaped rear.

clue.text: One trying to help animal round river

parts.note: a dog is an animal
O is round in shape
the Oder is a river in central Europe

explanation.surface: Someone tries to help a creature stranded around a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-meaning person who busily tries to improve others' lives.

clue.text: State of the heartless giant

definitions.meaning: in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, the cruel giant of Doubting Castle

explanation.surface: The condition of a cruel monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness is a state of mind, and Bunyan named his cruel giant after it.

clue.text: Each expert cages a bird like a crow-or a rook, possibly

indicators.note: cages means encloses, so the word for expert wraps the bird

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a pie, or magpie, is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: Each expert keeps a crow-like bird, or perhaps a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rook, possibly' reads as another bird, but a rook is a chess piece. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Per item, for every one; and a rook is one chessman.

clue.text: Manager of local eleven finally invested in popular defender

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the letter is placed within the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the last letter of eleven is the one taken

parts.note: a goalkeeper defends the goal

explanation.surface: A football team's manager picks a well-liked goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' is the British word for one's neighbourhood pub, not the football club the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a pub or inn, the local, is its landlord.

clue.text: Forcibly remove from famous theatre

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of famous theatre

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown out of a celebrated playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or expel by force is to drive out.

clue.text: What's put up without a break, by the way?

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written from the bottom upwards
without means lacking, so the A is dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Something built continuously, with no gaps, beside a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without a' takes A from BREAK to leave BREK, and 'put up' turns it to the answer. The definition: the edge stone lies by the roadway.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised edging of a pavement runs alongside the road.

clue.text: Actor having an edge in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word for sharp is heard

parts.note: something keen has a sharp edge

explanation.surface: An actor trying out for a part has the competitive edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Kean was a celebrated English Shakespearean actor of the early 1800s.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Kean was a famous tragic performer on the London stage.

clue.text: It's OK to walk fast with one friend

parts.note: leg it is British slang for run or walk quickly
I is the Roman numeral one
mate is British for friend

explanation.surface: Permission to hurry along with a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful or acceptable, all right by the rules.

clue.text: Take one boy round to see artist

indicators.note: turned round, the word for boy is read from the end back

parts.note: a lad is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes a young lad along to see a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' and 'to see' are links; Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: Flame could make hot bar hotter

definitions.text: Flame could make hot bar hotter

parts.words: Flame could make hot bar hotter
parts.note: flame looks like fire heating a bar, but here it is an old flame, a lover whose presence makes the room swelter

explanation.surface: A fire burning near a bar makes it hotter still.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol or sweetheart who sets pulses racing is a dreamy object of desire.
